subject: Human Body
title: Serotonin: Mood and Gut
description: A micro-lesson that makes Serotonin: Mood and Gut usable.

hook.text: 90% of your body's serotonin isn't in your brain. It's in your gut. The 'happiness chemical' mostly manages digestion.

buildup.text: In the brain, serotonin regulates mood, sleep, and appetite. Low serotonin is linked to depression and anxiety.

discovery.text: SSRIs (like Prozac) work by blocking serotonin reuptake, keeping more available in the brain.

twist.text: Gut bacteria produce serotonin precursors. Your microbiome directly influences your brain chemistry and emotional state.

climax.text: Serotonin connects gut health to mental health. The gut-brain axis means what you eat can literally change how you feel.

punchline.text: Your gut bacteria help make serotonin. Diet affects mood.

quiz.question: Where is most of the body's serotonin located?
